match.reason: The closest bank point, Global health inequities, is framed around life-expectancy gaps between countries and also covers water, sanitation and education, so it is broader than this point's focus on how poverty limits access to food, housing, health care and education.

rejected.title: Poverty
card: Poverty means a person or family lacks the resources to meet basic needs. It is often measured by income, but it affects far more than money.
Poverty limits access to enough nutritious food, safe housing, health care and education. Each of these shapes how healthy a person is.
These limits connect. Poor nutrition and crowded housing raise the risk of illness. Missing out on education can limit later work and income.
This can keep families in poverty across generations. Poverty therefore lowers both health and human development.
rejected.remember: Poverty limits food, housing, health care and education, and so lowers health and development.

a.q: How does poverty most directly lower a child's health?
opts: It limits access to food, housing and health care
It makes children less interested in learning
It stops governments from collecting any taxes
It means families choose to avoid medical care
a.why: Poverty limits access to the basics that support health, such as nutritious food, safe housing and health care. Saying families choose to avoid care is wrong, because the problem is lack of access, not choice.
a.clue: Think of the basic needs that poverty restricts.

b.q: Priya's family in rural Bihar cannot afford school fees, so she leaves school at 12. How does this show that poverty can persist across generations?
opts: Less education may limit her later income and options
She will no longer need nutritious food as an adult
Leaving school guarantees she will become ill later
Her family will gain access to better housing at once
b.why: Missing education can limit the work and income Priya can get later, which can leave her own children in poverty too. Leaving school does not guarantee illness. The card says it can limit options, not that outcomes are certain.
b.clue: Think about what education can lead to later in life.
